items.title: Google ships Gemini 4 Argon — output token limit jumps from 64K to 1M
items.summary: Argon is built for long-horizon professional work: software engineering, enterprise knowledge tasks, and vulnerability remediation. It sets a new state of the art on DeepSWE v1.1 (77.9%) and ranks #1 on AutomationBench (51.3%). The headline change is the output ceiling — up from 64K to 1M tokens. It's rolling out first to trusted cyber-defense partners via the Fairwind program, with broader API and Google AI Ultra access coming soon.
items.why: A 16x jump in how much a model can output in one shot means fewer long coding or research tasks get chopped off mid-thought — a different kind of capability than just being smarter per token.
items.action: Not broadly available yet — check your Gemini API console or AI Ultra access over the next week, then point your longest-running agent task at it first.

eval.reason: Output ceiling 64K to 1M plus new DeepSWE SOTA.
No first-party demo exists yet; omitted.
Biggest story of the day, with a direct long-horizon coding implication.

items.title: OpenAI ships GPT-6.1 Sol — matches flagship Astra on coding at one-fifth the cost
items.summary: On DeepSWE v1.1, Sol matches GPT-6 Astra's coding performance at roughly a fifth of the per-task cost, lands within 2 points of Astra on OSWorld 2.0, and cached input drops to $0.10 per million tokens. Available via the API as gpt-6.1-sol and in ChatGPT Work and Codex.
items.why: Near-flagship coding and computer-use capability becoming cheap enough to run constantly instead of sparingly changes how liberally you'd use an agent for routine work.
items.action: Point your next agentic coding task in Codex or the API at gpt-6.1-sol and compare — the cost difference is visible in one run.

eval.reason: Concrete capability-per-cost deltas, real API availability.

items.title: Uber cut AI agent costs 52% while usage grew 10x — the lever was a 24M-node context knowledge graph
items.summary: Uber split spend into users × sessions × turns × requests × tokens, protected adoption and attacked the agent's trajectory. The biggest lever: a 24M+ node graph linking 30+ internal systems that agents query instead of crawling the codebase cold — one question went from a wrong answer in 20 minutes to a correct one in 38 seconds.
items.why: A production version of exactly the problem a semantic code knowledge graph is supposed to solve — agents stop re-deriving context and start querying a structure that already has it.
items.action: Sketch what a queryable graph of your own services, PRs, and incident history would look like, and where an agent currently wastes tokens rediscovering that context.

eval.reason: Not a SHIPPED item, no demo-video requirement.
A production example of agents querying a context graph instead of re-deriving context.

items.title: CallPad's agents write and run their own evals against the live product — booking rate went from 35% to 65%
items.summary: Every call their AI receptionist gets wrong becomes a permanent regression test: agents write evals from live failures, replay them against the deployed system, and score with an LLM judge plus deterministic checks before a person merges.
items.why: A concrete blueprint for making sure an agent's production mistake can never silently happen again — without a human hand-writing the test.
items.action: Lift the pattern of agents generating eval cases from real failures and replaying them against the real system — not mocks — for any pipeline you gate merges on.

eval.reason: Concrete architecture with a measured outcome.
Not a SHIPPED item, no demo-video requirement.

items.title: OpenRig: a multi-agent harness that runs Claude Code and Codex together as one team
items.summary: Define a team in YAML, boot it with one command, and OpenRig manages persistent identity, shared context, and session coordination across Claude Code and Codex agents — including a "Claude owner + Codex checker" pair.
items.why: Having a second, differently-trained model check Claude Code's own diffs is a cheap way to catch the blind spots a single model has about its own output.
items.action: npx @openrig/cli init in a throwaway repo and stand up a Claude-owner / Codex-checker pod — ten minutes to see whether the second opinion catches anything.

eval.reason: Maintained multi-agent harness, not a wrapper.
Not a SHIPPED item, no demo-video requirement.
Pairs two widely used coding agents with a 10-minute setup.
